# @rootnative/seo — SEO for a React Native web export

> Version: 0.0.0-alpha.26
> Peer deps (/react and /expo-router only): react >=19.2.3 <20.0.0, react-native >=0.83.0 <0.87.0
> Optional peer dep (/expo-router only): expo-router >=57.0.0
> The core and /schema entries have no dependency; /node runs in Node only.

What a search engine and a link preview read from a React Native web app: the document head, the structured data, the heading outline, the image text, the HTML shell, the sitemap, and the robots file. Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/ui/seo/why

```bash
pnpm add @rootnative/seo
```

## The checklist, in order

1. **Static output.** `web.output: 'static'` in app.json, and `extra.router.sitemap: false` so `_sitemap.html` is not exported. A dynamic route needs `generateStaticParams`. `web.output: 'server'` writes the same HTML to `dist/server` and the files to `dist/client`; every `/node` function and command takes `dist` and reads that layout. The server sends a real 404 for an unknown path, sends a dynamic route template with a 200 for every slug (so an unknown entry needs `noindex`), and ignores `experiments.baseUrl`: host it at the origin root.
2. **Links as `Link`.** `Link` from expo-router renders `<a href>`. A `Pressable` with `router.push` renders a `<div>`, and a `Button` with `Linking.openURL` renders a `<button>`; a crawler follows neither. Put a component inside `<Link href asChild>`. On the web `Link` opens an external URL in the same tab; for a new tab pass `hrefAttrs={{ target: '_blank', rel: 'noopener' }}` to the component, because under `asChild` `Link` gives `target` to the child as a plain prop, which react-native-web drops.
3. **The head on every page.** `defineSite` once, `SeoProvider` at the root, `PageHead` on each screen, and `<RouteHead defaults={fn} />` after the navigator for the screen that has none: `defaults` maps the pathname to a `PageMeta`, and a `PageHead` on the route wins the whole page. A page with no `url` gets no canonical link and no share card, which is correct for a `noindex` overlay. A page in more than one language passes the same `alternates` list (`{ lang, url }[]`, every version, itself included) to the `PageHead` of each version. Every version keeps the `lang` of `app/+html.tsx`.
4. **Robots and sitemap.** Run `rootnative-seo dist` in the deploy step, after the export. It lists every exported page that has a canonical link under the site and no `noindex`, writes `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`, and prints each page it leaves out with the reason. `robots.txt` is read at the origin root only.
5. **Headings and `alt`.** `Typography` takes `level` (1..6) and renders `<h1>`..`<h6>`; a display or headline variant with no `level` is a plain element on the web. `Heading` from `/react` does the same for an app without `@rootnative/components`. One `<h1>` per page: the `AppBar` title is level 1 by default (`titleLevel` changes it), so put app headings at level 2 and below. Landmarks from `role`: one `<View role="main">` around the navigator in the root layout; `AppBar` is the `banner` and `NavigationBar`, `NavigationRail`, and the standard `NavigationDrawer` are `navigation` on their own. Set `lang` on `<html>` in `app/+html.tsx`. For an image a crawler must see, `Picture` from `/expo-image`: a plain `<img>` with `alt`, `width` and `height` on the web, `expo-image` on native. On an `expo-image` that stays, set both `alt` and `accessibilityLabel` and the `og:image` fallback; `imageLabel` builds the text.
6. **JSON-LD.** The builders in `@rootnative/seo/schema`; pass the result in `jsonLd`. An empty field is never written.
7. **Bundle and preconnect.** `shellTags` in `app/+html.tsx` with a `preconnect` per origin the first paint needs.
8. **The small tags.** Theme colour, icons and the manifest, through `shellTags` and `writeManifest`.

Check the export before you deploy: `rootnative-seo audit dist` reads every page and fails on a missing title, a page with no canonical link and no `noindex`, not exactly one `<h1>` or `<main>`, no `lang` on `<html>`, an `<img>` with no `alt`, `hreflang` links that the other language versions do not match, or a sitemap that disagrees with the pages. `rootnative-seo browse dist` then loads every page in headless Chrome and fails on an uncaught exception, a `console.error`, or a failed request, which is where a hydration mismatch shows. Lighthouse and Search Console on the live host are the only checks that count.

## `@rootnative/seo` — core (no dependency)

```ts
import { defineSite, toHeadTags, clipDescription, isoDuration, serializeJsonLd, resolveUrl } from '@rootnative/seo'
import type { PageMeta, PageAlternate, SiteConfig, Site, HeadTag, JsonLd, OpenGraphType } from '@rootnative/seo'
```

- `defineSite(config: SiteConfig): Site` — fills the defaults. Throws on an empty `name` or a relative `url`. Strips a trailing slash from `url`.
  - `SiteConfig`: `name`, `url` (absolute origin + base path), `locale?`, `titleTemplate?: (title) => string` (default `"<title> | <name>"`, and the bare name when the title equals it), `twitterSite?` (`@handle`), `descriptionLimit?` (default 160).
- `toHeadTags(site, meta: PageMeta): HeadTag[]` — tag records, not elements. Any head renderer can write them.
  - `PageMeta`: `title`, `description?`, `url?` (absolute or relative to the site), `image?: string | null`, `imageSize?: { width, height }`, `imageAlt?`, `type?: 'website' | 'article' | 'profile' | 'video.movie' | 'product'`, `locale?`, `noindex?`, `alternates?: PageAlternate[]`, `twitterCard?: 'summary' | 'summary_large_image'`, `jsonLd?: JsonLd[]`.
  - `PageAlternate`: `{ lang, url }`. `lang` is a BCP 47 code (`en`, `de-AT`) or `x-default`; `url` is absolute or relative to the site. List every language version, this page included, in the same order on each version.
  - `HeadTag`: `{ tag: 'title', text }` | `{ tag: 'meta', name, content }` | `{ tag: 'meta', property, content }` | `{ tag: 'link', rel, href, hreflang? }` | `{ tag: 'script', type: 'application/ld+json', text }`.
  - Rules: the tab title uses the template, `og:title` does not. No `url` → no canonical link and no og/twitter tags. `og:image:width`/`height` only with an image and an `imageSize`. Twitter card `summary_large_image` with an image, `summary` without, unless `twitterCard` forces one. `noindex` writes `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. `alternates` writes one `<link rel="alternate" hreflang href>` per entry after the canonical link, plus `x-default` with the URL of the first entry when the list has none, and only with a `url`. Each other tag is written once.
- `clipDescription(text, limit = 160)` — collapses whitespace, clips at a word boundary, adds one `…`.
- `isoDuration(minutes)` — `150` → `'PT2H30M'`. Returns `null` for `0`, a negative, or a non-finite number.
- `serializeJsonLd(value)` — `JSON.stringify` with every `<` as `\\u003c`, so `</script>` in a title cannot end the tag.
- `resolveUrl(site, pathOrUrl)` — joins a path under the site; an absolute URL passes through.
- `headTagsHtml(tags)` — the tags as HTML, one per line, escaped, for a static template such as the `index.html` of a Vite build: `template.replace('</head>', headTagsHtml(toHeadTags(site, meta)) + '</head>')`.

## `@rootnative/seo/schema` — JSON-LD builders (no dependency)

Each returns a `JsonLd` with `@context: 'https://schema.org'` and `@type` set. Every empty field (`undefined`, `null`, `""`, `[]`, `{}`) is removed at every depth.

- `webSite({ name, url, searchUrlTemplate? })` — adds a `SearchAction` with `query-input: 'required name=search_term_string'` when the template is set.
- `breadcrumbList(trail: { name, url }[])` — `ListItem`s with `position` from 1.
- `organization({ name, url, logo?, sameAs? })`
- `article({ headline, url, image?, description?, datePublished?, dateModified?, author? })` — `author` is a string or `{ name, url? }`, written as a `Person`. Sets `mainEntityOfPage` to `url`.
- `product({ name, url, image?, description?, brand?, sku?, offers?, aggregateRating? })` — `brand` becomes `Brand`; `offers: { price, priceCurrency, availability?, url? }` becomes `Offer` with `availability` as `https://schema.org/<name>`.
- `movie({ name, url, image?, description?, datePublished?, genre?, durationMinutes?, actors?, director?, rating? })` — `duration` through `isoDuration`; `actors` and `director` as `Person`.
- `person({ name, url, image?, description?, birthDate?, deathDate?, birthPlace?, jobTitle?, sameAs? })` — `birthPlace` as `Place`.
- `event({ name, url, startDate, endDate?, location?, image?, description? })` — `location` is a string or `{ name, address? }`, as `Place`.
- `faqPage(questions: { question, answer }[])` — `Question` + `Answer` under `mainEntity`.
- `RatingInput`: `{ ratingValue, ratingCount?, reviewCount?, bestRating? (5), worstRating? (1) }`. A rating with no count is left out.

## `@rootnative/seo/react` — peers: react `>=19.2.3 <20.0.0`, react-native `>=0.83.0 <0.87.0`

- `<SeoProvider site={site}>` — gives every `PageHead` and `RouteHead` below it the site, and tracks which route a `PageHead` claims.
- `useSite(site?)` — the site for the tree. A `site` argument wins. Throws with no provider and no argument.
- `<Heading level={1..6} as={Component}>` — renders the given text component (default RN `Text`) with `accessibilityRole="header"` and `aria-level`. On the web react-native-web writes `<h1>`..`<h6>`. Generic: `<Heading<TypographyProps> level={2} as={Typography} variant="titleMedium">`. The wrapped component's own `as`, `role`, `accessibilityRole` and `aria-level` props are omitted.
- `imageLabel(kind, subject?)` — `imageLabel('Poster', 'Dune')` → `'Dune poster'`. Set the result as both `alt` and `accessibilityLabel` on `expo-image` (its web `alt` comes from `accessibilityLabel`).

## `@rootnative/seo/expo-router` — optional peer: expo-router `>=57.0.0`

- `<PageHead {...meta} site?>` — `PageMeta` as props, plus an optional `site` that wins over the provider. Writes the tags through `expo-router/head`. On native it renders `null` and reads no site, so a native tree or test needs no `SeoProvider`. On the web a missing site throws, and the static export fails.
- `<RouteHead defaults={(pathname) => PageMeta | undefined} site?>` — for the root layout, after the navigator. Writes the head of the current route when no focused screen on it renders a `PageHead`; a `PageHead` wins the whole page, not one tag at a time. `undefined` writes nothing. Native renders `null`. Put it after the navigator: the screen renders first and claims the route, and the static export runs no effect. Before the navigator, the export holds both heads, and the component warns in development.
- `renderHeadTag(tag, index)` — one `HeadTag` as the element `expo-router/head` expects. A JSON-LD script is written as a string child, not `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (react-helmet-async drops the latter).
- `shellTags(options): ReactElement[]` — for `app/+html.tsx`: charset, viewport (default `width=device-width, initial-scale=1, shrink-to-fit=no`), `themeColor`, `favicon`, `appleTouchIcon`, `manifest`, `preconnect: { href, crossOrigin? }[]`. `themeColor` is a string or `{ light, dark }`; the object form writes one `theme-color` tag per `prefers-color-scheme`, which follows the system scheme, not a mode picked in the app. `basePath` (pass `process.env.EXPO_BASE_URL`) prefixes every relative `href`. No router dependency: works in a Vite template through `renderToStaticMarkup`. Expo Router writes the `PageHead` tags before the shell, so the charset can land after byte 1024: the host must send `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`.

## `@rootnative/seo/dom` — peers: react, react-native; no router

- `<PageHead {...meta} site? active?>` — the same `PageMeta` props as the Expo Router `PageHead`, for an app with no Expo Router: React Navigation on react-native-web, a Vite build, an Electron renderer. Writes the `toHeadTags` records to `document.head` in an effect and takes them out on unmount, so the two adapters write the same head. A tag of the same name, property or `rel` that was there before, from the template or from a screen below, is taken out while this head is on and put back when it goes, and the `hreflang` links go as one set, so no language of the head below stays: a screen mounted over another wins, and the one below gets its head back. `active={false}` takes the head out for a screen that stays mounted behind another; a React Navigation screen passes `useIsFocused()`. Native renders `null`. An effect never runs on a server, so a static file gets its head from `headTagsHtml` at build time.

## `@rootnative/seo/expo-image` — optional peer: expo-image `>=57.0.0`

- `<Picture source alt width height contentFit? loading? site? style? testID?>` — an image a crawler sees. On the web a plain `<img>` with `src`, `alt`, `width`, `height`, `loading` (default `lazy`), `decoding="async"` and `object-fit` from `contentFit` (default `cover`); on native `expo-image` with `alt` and `accessibilityLabel`. `source` is absolute, or a path under the site URL like `PageMeta.image`: the web gets the path under the host, native the absolute URL, and a relative one needs the site from `SeoProvider` or the `site` prop. `style` is a React Native image style that comes after the `width` and `height` box, so a size in `style` wins; set a side to `undefined` to let `flex` or `aspectRatio` size it. The web lays out the `<img>` as a react-native-web view, and flattens the style to CSS. `alt=""` marks a decorative image.

## `@rootnative/seo/node` — Node only, no peer

- `rootnative-seo <outDir> [--site-url <url>] [--sitemap <url>]... [--no-robots]` — the command for the deploy step, after the export. It runs `writeSeoFiles`, prints each page it leaves out with the reason, and exits with 1 on an error. `--sitemap` replaces the sitemap list in `robots.txt`; repeat it for more than one.
- `writeSeoFiles({ outDir, siteUrl?, robots? })` — reads every `.html` file under `outDir` and writes `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` there. A server export, which has `server/_expo/routes.json` and `client/`, is read from `<outDir>/server`, and the two files go to `<outDir>/client`, the folder the server sends as files; every `/node` function below reads the same layout. A page goes in the sitemap with its canonical link, when the link is under the site and the page has no `noindex`. Left out, with a `reason`: a special route (a `+` or `_` segment, or a root `404.html`), a dynamic route template (`[id].html`), `noindex`, no canonical link, a canonical link outside the site, and a second page with the same link. A page with `hreflang` links gets the same links as `xhtml:link` entries. `siteUrl` defaults to the canonical link of `index.html`. `robots: false` writes no `robots.txt`; an object passes options to `writeRobots`. Resolves to `{ siteUrl, sitemap, robots?, urls, skipped: { file, reason }[] }`. Each sitemap entry holds `loc` only: Google ignores `changefreq` and `priority`, and an export does not know `lastmod`. Throws when no page can go in the sitemap, because an empty sitemap fails with no other signal.
- `readExport(outDir)` — `{ file, route, canonical?, noindex, alternates: { lang, url }[] }[]` for every exported HTML file, sorted by path. Use it to build a URL list of your own.
- `rootnative-seo audit <outDir> [--site-url <url>] [--ignore <rule>]...` — the gate for CI, after the export and after `rootnative-seo <outDir>`. It runs `auditExport`, prints each problem with its file and rule, and exits with 1 when there is one. It writes nothing. `--ignore` skips one rule; repeat it for more.
- `auditExport({ outDir, siteUrl?, ignore? })` — reads every `.html` file under `outDir` and returns `{ pages, problems: { file, rule, message }[] }`. The rules: `title` (one `<title>` with text), `canonical` (an absolute canonical link, or `noindex`), `h1` (exactly one `<h1>`), `main` (exactly one `<main>`), `lang` (a `lang` on `<html>`), `alt` (every `<img>` has an `alt` attribute), `hreflang` (on each indexable page with `hreflang` links: every code is a language code or `x-default`, not `-UK`; every link is absolute; one link per code; a link to the page itself; every linked page in the export has a file, no `noindex`, and the same set; and the `xhtml:link` entries of the sitemap, when it has them, are the links of the page), and `sitemap` (`sitemap.xml` exists, every `<loc>` is the canonical link of a page, and every page `writeSeoFiles` would list is in it). `siteUrl` defaults to the canonical link of `index.html`; with neither, the second half of the `sitemap` rule is skipped. An empty `problems` list is a pass. It throws only when the folder is missing or holds no HTML file.
- `rootnative-seo browse <outDir> [--chrome <path>] [--base-path <path>] [--settle <ms>]` — the second gate for CI, after the export. It runs `browseExport`, prints each problem with its file and kind, and exits with 1 when there is one. It writes nothing. Chrome comes from `--chrome`, then `CHROME_PATH`, then the usual names on `PATH` and the usual install paths.
- `browseExport({ outDir, basePath?, chrome?, settleMs?, timeoutMs? })` — serves `outDir` and loads every `.html` file in headless Chrome, driven over its debugging pipe with no package. Returns `{ pages, problems: { file, route, kind, message }[], chrome }`, where `kind` is `exception` (uncaught), `console` (`console.error` or `console.assert`), or `log` (a browser log entry, such as a request that failed). A hydration mismatch is a `console.error` in development and a reported error in production, so both reach the list. `settleMs` (default 750) is how long it listens after the load event, so hydration runs. Throws when no Chrome is found, the folder is missing, it holds no HTML file, or the scripts of `index.html` are not under the base path. That last message names both paths, so a base-path mismatch is one line, not a failed request for each script on each page.
- `serveExport({ outDir, basePath?, port? })` — serves `outDir` on `127.0.0.1` as a static host serves an Expo Router export (a server export: a file from `client/`, then a page from `server/`, never the route manifest; a dynamic route gets its own file only, where the Expo server sends the template for every slug): `/about` is `about.html` or `about/index.html`, a route with no file gets `+not-found.html` or `404.html` with status 404, and a request outside `outDir` is refused. `basePath` defaults to the path of the canonical link of `index.html`. Resolves to `{ origin, basePath, urlOf(route), close() }`. Use it to run Lighthouse or a browser test on the export.
- `findChrome(path?)` — the Chrome or Chromium binary `browseExport` would use, or `undefined`.

The three functions below write one file each. Each creates `outDir`, writes the file and resolves to its path. Each has a pure sibling that returns the text.

- `writeSitemap({ outDir, siteUrl, urls, fileName? })` / `sitemapXml({ siteUrl, urls })` — `urls: { loc, lastmod?, changefreq?, priority?, alternates? }[]`. A relative `loc` or alternate `url` is joined under `siteUrl`. `alternates` become `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang href>` entries, and `<urlset>` declares the `xhtml` namespace only then. Every value is XML-escaped. `priority` is clamped to 0..1.
- `writeRobots({ outDir, sitemapUrl, disallow?, allow?, userAgent?, fileName? })` / `robotsTxt(...)` — `sitemapUrl` is one URL or a list. With no `disallow` the file allows everything. The file carries a comment that says why an overlay route is not disallowed: a crawler reads `noindex` only on a page it may fetch.
- `writeManifest({ outDir, name, shortName?, description?, startUrl? ('./'), scope? ('./'), display? ('standalone'), themeColor?, backgroundColor?, lang?, icons?, fileName? })` / `manifestJson(...)` — relative paths, so it works under a subpath host. The icon `type` is inferred from the file extension.
